args.text: When the description presents multiple alternative ways to implement a solution, model each alternative as a separate task on mutually exclusive branches, using exclusive gateways to split and merge the alternatives.

trace.reason: Check whether existing documented guidance already covers modeling explicit alternatives as exclusive branches.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use an exclusive merge for alternative paths; it does not wait for inactive alternatives.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.

args.text: When the description lists alternative ways to carry out an outcome, model each alternative as a separate activity on mutually exclusive branches controlled by an exclusive gateway.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers modeling explicitly stated alternatives.

result.rule: When the description presents two or more distinct activities as alternatives: Model each activity as a separate task on its own branch rather than combining the alternatives into one task; choose a gateway that matches whether one or multiple alternatives may be performed.

When the description presents mutually alternative ways to signal the same need and identifies a shared subsequent activity.: Model the alternatives as exclusive branches and merge them before the shared activity.

When the description says that an item is placed in one of multiple alternative destinations: Model the alternatives with an exclusive gateway and a separate task for each destination, rather than one combined task.

When the description says an activity may or may not occur before a later required activity: model the optional activity as one branch of an exclusive gateway, and merge the branches before the later required activity

args.text: When naming BPMN tasks and events, use concise labels that faithfully express the action or outcome stated in the process description. Avoid adding unnecessary detail or expanding labels into sentences.

trace.reason: Check whether existing documented guidance addresses concise, description-faithful element labels.

result.rule: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Declare the BPMN model namespace http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL and a non-empty targetNamespace on bpmn:definitions.
